question: What is the very first check a nurse must perform before giving any medication?

options.A: Check the expiration date on the medication packaging
options.B: Verify the patient's identity using two unique identifiers
options.C: Ask the doctor if the prescription is still valid
options.D: Measure the patient's current vital signs

explanation: Ensuring you have the correct person is the primary safeguard in healthcare before administering any treatment. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is recording a medication administration immediately after giving it so important?

options.A: It proves to the patient that the nurse is working efficiently
options.B: It allows the pharmacy to automatically restock the item
options.C: It prevents another nurse from accidentally giving the same dose
options.D: It satisfies hospital accreditation rules without clinical benefit

explanation: Prompt charting creates a clear real-time record that protects the patient from receiving a dangerous double dose. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the safest way to check if a patient has drug allergies before giving a medication?

options.A: Trust that the pharmacy filtered out all possible allergens
options.B: Ask a family member if the patient has any food preferences
options.C: Check the chart, look at the allergy band, and ask the patient directly
options.D: Review only the physical allergy band on the bed frame

explanation: Using multiple checks like the chart, band, and talking to the patient ensures nothing gets missed. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h2)

question: A patient is due for digoxin, but their pulse is 52 beats per minute. What should you do?

options.A: Crush the tablet to speed up its absorption in the stomach
options.B: Hold the medication and notify the prescribing physician
options.C: Give half the dose now and the other half later in the day
options.D: Administer the medication with a glass of orange juice

explanation: Great clinical instinct! Digoxin slows the heart down, so a pulse below 60 means it's safer to hold the drug and call the doctor. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h2)

question: At which three moments should a nurse check a medication label?

options.A: Opening the box, crushing the pill, and charting
options.B: Retrieving it, preparing it, and at the bedside
options.C: At the pharmacy, in the hallway, and at discharge
options.D: During shift handover, before lunch, and at night

explanation: Spot on! Checking the label at these three key steps helps you catch any errors before the drug gets to the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is it dangerous to administer a medication prepared by another nurse?

options.A: It takes away valuable learning time from student nurses
options.B: The pharmacy software will crash when scanning the barcode
options.C: You cannot verify its true contents or preparation accuracy
options.D: It violates hospital laundry and uniform policies

explanation: The person who prepares the medication must be the one who administers it to maintain complete safety accountability. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why does an intravenous (IV) medication work much faster than a swallowed pill?

options.A: It travels straight to the liver for immediate activation
options.B: It is manufactured using higher chemical concentrations
options.C: It avoids the lungs where oxygen slows down circulation
options.D: It enters the bloodstream directly without needing absorption

explanation: Exactly! Because IV meds skip the digestive tract and go straight into the blood, they start working almost instantly. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which medication route involves placing a tablet under the tongue to dissolve?
explanation: Sublingual medications dissolve under the tongue where rich blood vessels allow quick absorption into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the main legal risk if a nurse forgets to document a medication right after giving it?

options.A: The hospital computer system will delete the patient file
options.B: The pharmacy will automatically double the next scheduled dose
options.C: The patient's insurance company will refuse to pay the bill
options.D: Legally, the medication is considered unadministered

explanation: In nursing law, if it isn't charted, it didn't happen! Always document promptly to protect your license and your patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h5)

question: What should a nurse do when a patient refuses to take a prescribed oral medication?

options.A: Document the refusal and notify the prescribing doctor
options.B: Hide the crushed pill inside sweet food without telling them
options.C: Force the medication gently by holding the patient's jaw
options.D: Leave the pill on the bedside table for them to take later

explanation: Competent patients have the right to refuse treatment, and the care team must be informed to adjust the plan. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse must do after discovering a medication error?

options.A: Call the hospital lawyer to explain what happened
options.B: Fill out the institutional incident report form right away
options.C: Assess the patient's vital signs and current physical condition
options.D: Hide the medication packaging so nobody notices the mistake

explanation: Patient well-being always comes first! Always check your patient's condition before worrying about paperwork. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent medication errors?

options.A: Minimizing hallway conversations while calculating doses
options.B: Double-checking high-alert calculations with a colleague
options.C: Carefully reading medication labels three separate times
options.D: Rushing through drug rounds to finish ahead of schedule

explanation: Spot on! Rushing causes stress and mistakes. Taking your time is key to safe medication administration. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h6)
